panels.title: Two successions in twenty months
ascii_lines: SHASTRI PM -> JUNE 1964, after Nehru's death
1965 WAR -> India-Pakistan; ends at TASHKENT DECLARATION, Jan 1966
SHASTRI DIES -> Tashkent, 10 JANUARY 1966, hours after signing
INDIRA ELECTED PM -> JANUARY 1966, defeats Morarji Desai 355-169 (Syndicate-backed)
source_references: Shastri's accession and the 1965 war, June 1964 to January 1966
Indira Gandhi's election as Prime Minister, January 1966

panels.title: The mid-1960s economic crisis and the 1966 devaluation
ascii_lines: 1965 WAR EXPENDITURE + HARVEST FAILURES + FOOD-AID DEPENDENCE -> fiscal strain
RUPEE DEVALUED -> JUNE 1966, by about 35.5 per cent
POLITICAL COST -> blamed on Indira Gandhi within months of taking office
LEGACY -> durable aversion to externally pressed adjustment, until 1991
source_references: The rupee devaluation of June 1966 and its causes

panels.title: 1967: the end of easy dominance
ascii_lines: FOURTH GENERAL ELECTION -> 1967
CONGRESS -> majority SLASHED nationally; loses power in EIGHT STATES
NEW PATTERN -> Samyukta Vidhayak Dal (SVD) coalition governments
MASS DEFECTION -> "Aya Ram Gaya Ram"; about 800 legislators switch, 1967-70
source_references: The 1967 general election: the end of easy dominance
Coalition governments and defection politics after 1967

panels.title: 1969: the Congress split
ascii_lines: TRIGGER -> V.V. Giri presidential contest + bank nationalisation (14 banks)
SPLIT -> Congress (R), Indira Gandhi   vs   Congress (O), the Syndicate
OUTCOME -> most Congress MPs and the AICC side with Indira Gandhi
RESULT -> numbers held for Congress (R); party organisation did not
source_references: The 1969 Congress split: Giri, bank nationalisation and the Syndicate's defeat

panels.title: Courts vs the executive, 1970
ascii_lines: SUPREME COURT, 1970 -> strikes down FIRST bank-nationalisation order
SUPREME COURT, 1970 -> strikes down privy-purse DERECOGNITION order
GOVERNMENT RESPONSE -> re-enacts bank nationalisation via fresh legislation
GOVERNMENT RESPONSE -> abolishes privy purses via 26th Amendment, 1971
source_references: The Supreme Court's 1970 rulings against the executive

panels.title: 1971: privy purses and Garibi Hatao
ascii_lines: PRIVY PURSES ABOLISHED -> 1971, 26th Constitutional Amendment
1971 GENERAL ELECTION -> Congress (R) wins 352 of 518 seats
SLOGAN -> "Garibi Hatao"
READ IT CORRECTLY -> a NATIONAL plebiscite, delinked from state-level Congress
source_references: 1971: privy purses abolished and the Garibi Hatao landslide

panels.title: The 1971 Bangladesh war
ascii_lines: ORIGIN -> crisis in East Pakistan; refugee influx into India
OUTCOME -> decisive Indian military victory
RESULT -> creation of Bangladesh
EFFECT -> Indira Gandhi's domestic authority becomes unassailable
source_references: The 1971 Bangladesh war and its strategic significance

panels.title: 1965 vs 1971 compared
ascii_lines: 1965 WAR -> origin: Pakistani infiltration into Kashmir
1965 WAR -> outcome: militarily inconclusive; ends at Tashkent Declaration
1971 WAR -> origin: East Pakistan refugee crisis
1971 WAR -> outcome: decisive victory; creates Bangladesh
source_references: Comparing 1965 and 1971: two wars, two outcomes

panels.title: Pokhran-I, May 1974
ascii_lines: TEST -> Pokhran-I, MAY 1974
OFFICIAL LABEL -> "peaceful nuclear explosion", not a declared weapons test
SIGNIFICANCE -> first Indian nuclear test; inside the Garibi-Hatao-to-Emergency arc
TRAP -> do not date this test to the 1960s
source_references: Pokhran-I, May 1974: India's first nuclear test

panels.title: De-institutionalisation: the hidden cost
ascii_lines: TECHNIQUE -> populist mobilisation + personalised leadership
EFFECT ON PARTY -> Congress organisation split and weakened after 1969
EFFECT ON CHECKS -> internal factional-conflict checks eroded
LONGER EFFECT -> structural background to the 1973-75 crisis
source_references: De-institutionalisation: the hidden cost of consolidation

panels.title: The coal-sector nationalisation gap, 2019: a bounded caution
ascii_lines: ROUTED DEMAND -> 2019 Prelims GS-I Q48, coal-sector nationalisation status
LOCAL SUPPORT -> NONE in any modern-history source book in this repository
RULE -> no year, statute or sequence for coal nationalisation stated from memory
ACTION -> route any full answer to the Economy or Geography owner instead
source_references: The coal-sector nationalisation gap: a bounded caution

panels.title: Resilience and cost: two verdicts on 1964-73
ascii_lines: VERDICT ONE -> resilience: two successions absorbed peacefully; 1971 war won
VERDICT TWO -> cost: party de-institutionalised; internal democracy eroded
CHANDRA'S READING -> the leftward turn was genuine, if organisationally costly
SYNTHESIS -> both readings are compatible, not competing, accounts of the decade
source_references: Resilience and cost: two verdicts on 1964-73

panels.title: The 1972-73 economic crisis
ascii_lines: TWIN MONSOON FAILURES + 1973 OIL SHOCK -> deepening scarcity
PRICE RISE -> about 22 per cent over 1972-73
EFFECT -> inflation, unemployment, food scarcity erode Indira Gandhi's popularity
TIMING -> follows directly on the 1971 Garibi Hatao landslide
source_references: The 1972-73 economic crisis: drought, inflation and the oil shock

panels.title: Nav Nirman and the Bihar movement, 1974
ascii_lines: NAV NIRMAN -> Gujarat, JANUARY 1974; students protest prices and corruption
BIHAR MOVEMENT -> MARCH 1974; JP takes leadership
JP'S CALL -> "Total Revolution" / Sampoorna Kranti
SPREAD -> student unrest becomes a nationwide anti-government movement
source_references: Nav Nirman: the Gujarat student agitation, January 1974
The Bihar movement and JP's Total Revolution, March 1974

panels.title: The railway strike, May 1974
ascii_lines: ALL-INDIA RAILWAY STRIKE -> MAY 1974, lasting 22 days
DIRECT CHALLENGE -> to the government's authority
ADDED DIMENSION -> economic disruption layered onto the political crisis
CONTEXT -> deepens the crisis JP's movement was already building on
source_references: The railway strike of May 1974

panels.title: The Allahabad High Court judgment, 12 June 1975
ascii_lines: PETITIONER -> Raj Narain
JUDGE -> Justice Jagmohanlal Sinha, Allahabad High Court
DATE -> 12 JUNE 1975
RULING -> sets aside Indira Gandhi's 1971 election on electoral malpractice
source_references: The Allahabad High Court judgment, 12 June 1975

panels.title: The Supreme Court's conditional stay, 24 June 1975
ascii_lines: COURT -> Supreme Court, Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer
DATE -> 24 JUNE 1975
RULING -> CONDITIONAL stay of the Allahabad verdict
EFFECT -> Indira Gandhi remains Prime Minister while the appeal is pending
source_references: The Supreme Court's conditional stay, 24 June 1975

panels.title: The proclamation: dated 25 June, announced 26 June
ascii_lines: JP'S DELHI RALLY -> 25 JUNE 1975; calls for civil disobedience
PROCLAMATION -> Article 352, DATED 25 JUNE 1975
PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENT -> only on 26 JUNE 1975
TRAP -> the two dates must never be collapsed into one
source_references: JP's 25 June rally and the proclamation of Emergency

panels.title: Instruments of the Emergency: MISA, censorship, 42nd Amendment
ascii_lines: DETENTIONS -> under MISA; over 100,000 held without trial, ~19 months
PRESS -> censorship imposed
CONSTITUTIONAL CHANGE -> 42nd Amendment, 1976; expands central/executive power
AGENDA -> Twenty-Point Programme, 1 July 1975
source_references: The Emergency's legal instruments: MISA, censorship and the 42nd Amendment

panels.title: Sanjay Gandhi's extra-constitutional power and its excesses
ascii_lines: POSITION -> no formal office; extra-constitutional power centre
PROGRAMME -> his own four-point programme, 1976
EXCESSES -> compulsory sterilisation drives
EXCESSES -> slum-demolition drives
source_references: Sanjay Gandhi's extra-constitutional power and its excesses

panels.title: 1977: the electoral reversal
ascii_lines: ELECTIONS CALLED -> January 1977
ELECTIONS HELD -> March 1977
RESULT -> Congress and Sanjay Gandhi defeated
MEANING -> a verdict FOR civil liberties; ends the Emergency
source_references: The 1977 elections and the Emergency's end

panels.title: What held and what failed
ascii_lines: HELD -> the electoral machinery itself; free verdict delivered in 1977
FAILED -> Parliament; failed to check the executive
FAILED -> the ruling party; offered no internal restraint
FAILED -> judiciary's detention jurisprudence, in the MISA cases
source_references: What held and what failed: a balanced verdict

panels.title: The JP movement's social base
ascii_lines: BASE -> students, middle class, traders, intelligentsia
NOT THE BASE -> rural poor or the organised urban working class
STRENGTH -> moral authority sufficient to destabilise the government
LIMITATION -> no base broad enough to govern after 1977
source_references: The JP movement's social base: strength and limitation

ascii_lines: EVENT -> Union Cabinet resolution, 25 JUNE 2025
CONTENT -> commemorates fifty years since the Emergency
FRAMING -> honours resistance; reaffirms constitutional democracy
SOURCE -> PIB, PRID 2139543 (no public URL recorded by the owner)
